However, the adoption could come with environmental tradeoffs, particularly increased water consumption. This highlights the need for further research to optimize water consumption in biomass conversion processes alongside strategies to reduce WTP CAP emissions. These factors will impact the feasibility and adoption of alternative fuels in the rail locomotive industry. 60 6 ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH AND SAFETY When considering new fuels for implementation, it is important to understand and account for the environmental health and safety implications for the identified fuels, both positive and negative. The year 1 activities for this project identified that ammonia posed the greatest risks for human populations due to its toxicity compared to all other fuels under consideration. Those efforts focused specifically on two significant externalities for biofuel processing facilities: risk of chemical accident from ammonia processing facilities and traffic increases from feedstock shipments to ethanol and BD processing facilities. The results of that modeling highlighted the importance of release modeling with human population data and suggested that certain sites have a higher level of risk associated with their location, related to local population density. This type of analysis can help eliminate high risk sites from consideration. In addition to the potential danger posed by such a spill, the damage could harm public acceptance of biofuel facilities and of emerging fuels that can help with future cost reductions and resiliency. A recent report by Kolodziejczyk on the environmental and health issues of ammonia for transportation applications summarized the health and safety concerns and ammonia safety requirements (Kolodziejczyk, 2021). A thorough summary was completed for these same alternative fuels for the marine sector by Kass et al. (2021) for the U.S. DOT Maritime Administration. In year 2 of the project, an additional review of the literature for the alternative fuels under consideration was performed. This is summarized in Table 6-1.
